results.reason: The circuit captures what the bars look like and how to label each one, but makes the first clause a complement of “label” instead of the reason for the directive.
The imperative and object are present, but quantity=120 conflicts with the singular object introduced by “a.”
The circuit captures the dislike of the short cut and the instruction to give long hair instead, but encodes the second “her” only as a determiner and omits the recipient of “give.”
The particle “off,” object “this,” and with-phrase are present, but the subjectless participial fragment is marked as a declarative clause.
The circuit preserves “this” and the with-phrase, but treats the participial fragment as an imperative and the particle “off” as a result complement.
The circuit preserves the mouth, the target 1.1, and both verbs, but gives “enlarge” declarative form and “compare” imperative form even though both are coordinated bare verbs under “let’s.”
The circuit captures the polite deletion request and the instruction to leave moon alone, but classifies the contrastive “but” as additive.
The plant and the underneath relation are present, but treating “I'd” as a name loses the speaker and the modal “would” in the expression of preference.
The circuit classifies setting the highlights as placement and leaving the shadows alone as change. It also splits the target color “deep rose” into unrelated slots.

The circuit links the cat and “no more” as jointly governed by “of” in “on top of.” This misattaches the quantity limit, although the pair of cats and the instruction to keep the arrangement for the rest of the scene are present.
The causative imperative links to a looking clause whose subject is the bear in the woods and whose target is the pond.
